title.from: AI-translated pages say so to readers and agents
title.to: AI-translated pages say so to readers and agents, and quotations show their original

description.from:
As a reader or an agent, I want every translated page to say it was translated by AI from a linked original and whether a person reviewed it, so I know what I am reading.

Readers: a plain line under the byline in the page's language, linking the original. Agents: JSON-LD inLanguage, translationOfWork and translator; Markdown twin front matter language, translatedFrom, translation: machine, reviewed; llms.txt and the agent guide explain it. Translated quotations are marked and show the original wording. Plan: docs/plans/multilingual-publishing.md (PR #1450).

Feature: Translation labels

Scenario: A reader sees the label
  Given a published Spanish localization reviewed by a person
  When a reader opens it
  Then a line under the byline says it was translated by AI from the English original and reviewed, with a link to the original

Scenario: An agent reads the label
  Given the same page
  When an agent requests its Markdown twin
  Then the front matter names the language, the original URL, machine translation and reviewed true

Scenario: A translated quotation shows its original
  Given an English quotation in the original
  When the Spanish page renders it
  Then it is marked as translated and the original wording is available beside it
description.to:
As a reader or an agent, I want every translated page to say it was translated by AI from a linked original, and whether a person has reviewed it, so I know what I am reading.

Readers: a plain line under the byline in the page's language linking the original; it changes to 'translated by AI and reviewed by a person' once a corrector reviews the current version. Agents: JSON-LD inLanguage, translationOfWork, translator; Markdown twin language, translatedFrom, translation: machine, reviewed; llms.txt explains it. Quotations (Ryan's decision 9): translated, marked as translated, original one tap away (expand on touch, tooltip on hover, keyboard reachable, lang set), original kept in the quote's source-language field for agents; never a machine translation shown as a verbatim quote without the mark. Plan: docs/plans/multilingual-publishing.md (PR #1450), revised 2026-11-12 with Ryan's decisions.

Feature: Translation labels

Scenario: An unreviewed translation
  Given a published Spanish localization no corrector has reviewed
  When a reader opens it
  Then a line under the byline says it was translated by AI from the English original, with a link

Scenario: A reviewed translation
  Given a corrector pressed Looks right on the current Spanish version
  When a reader opens it
  Then the line says it was translated by AI and reviewed by a person

Scenario: An agent reads the label
  Given a published Spanish localization
  When an agent requests its Markdown twin
  Then the front matter names the language, the original URL, machine translation and whether it was reviewed

Scenario: A translated quotation
  Given an English quotation in the original
  When the Spanish page renders it
  Then it is marked as translated and the original wording opens with one tap
